fact: The PPRA said it is working with the Ministry of Finance to develop a national e-procurement system for real-time tracking of tenders.

The Finance Ministry's Permanent Secretary launched the PPADB Integrated Procurement Management System in July 2016, letting contractors register, download tender documents and submit online, with e-bidding modules in phase two.

The PPRA chief executive told the National Public Procurement Pitso that Botswana lacks a fully integrated e-procurement platform and runs manual processes, with government committed to launching a national e-procurement system by 2027.

PPRA chief executive Tumelo Motsumi said in a December 2025 media briefing that the absence of an e-procurement system makes compliance monitoring expensive and inefficient, and that records are kept in a manual system.

Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe told Parliament that the manual procurement system would be substituted with an e-procurement procedure, and Public Procurement Regulatory Authority IT systems would be developed.
